style: Style: an original illustration in the manner of an 18th-century Siamese manuscript painting (samut khoi folding book) and Ayutthaya-era temple mural line art: fine black ink contour lines, flat areas of a few natural pigments only (red ochre, indigo, muted green, touches of gold leaf, chalk white), on warm aged khoi-paper texture with soft stains. Head-and-shoulders bust, three-quarter view, centred, facing slightly left, dignified and respectful. Plain aged-paper background fading to the edges, no scenery. Any sword is a Siamese daab: straight wrapped hilt, small round pommel, no square or round Japanese-style guard. Historically plausible late-18th-century Siamese dress and hairstyle (short-cropped mahat-thai hair). Not photorealistic, not anime, not a game character. No text, no letters, no seals, no signature, no border.

items.taksin_general: Phraya Tak (later King Taksin) at about 33, a Siamese general of Thai-Chinese (Teochew) descent: lean, determined face, calm resolute eyes, short-cropped hair, thin moustache; wearing a fitted long-sleeved Siamese noble military jacket in deep red with a gold-trimmed collar over a dark sash, the hilt of a Siamese daab sword at his shoulder.
items.taksin_king: King Taksin of Thonburi at about 35, dignified and composed, short-cropped hair, thin moustache; wearing a tall pointed Siamese royal crown of gold (chada style) and a gold-brocade royal jacket with ornate shoulder pieces; a serene, resolute expression; depicted with great respect, as in a royal temple mural.
items.ruang: Chao Phraya Phitsanulok (named Ruang), a Siamese provincial governor in his late forties: broad, heavy-set face, proud and confident expression, short-cropped greying hair; wearing a dark green noble jacket with gold trim and a white sash.
items.fang: Chao Phra Fang (named Ruean), a Buddhist monk who led a northern Siamese faction, in his fifties: shaven head, thin stern face, intense eyes; wearing a saffron-ochre monk robe draped over one shoulder; austere and severe, depicted respectfully.
items.thepphiphit: Prince Thep Phiphit, a prince of the Ayutthaya royal house in his fifties: refined, aristocratic face with a slight weariness, short grey hair; wearing a tall conical Siamese court hat (lomphok) of white cloth with a gold band and an embroidered court jacket in indigo.
items.nakhon_nu: Chao Nakhon (named Nu), the ruler of Nakhon Si Thammarat in southern Siam, in his forties: sun-darkened weathered face, keen eyes, short-cropped hair, short beard; wearing a light patterned southern-style jacket and a red sash.
items.thongin: Nai Thong-in, a Siamese official placed in charge of Thonburi by the Burmese in 1767, in his thirties: anxious, uneasy expression, short-cropped hair; wearing a plain brown official jacket.
items.chinese_merchant: A Teochew Chinese junk merchant trading with Siam in the 1760s, in his forties: shaved forehead with a long Qing-dynasty queue, small black skullcap, thin moustache, shrewd friendly eyes; wearing a blue silk merchant robe, holding a wooden abacus.
items.chakri: Chao Phraya Chakri (Thong Duang), a Siamese general at about 39: strong, composed face, steady wise eyes, short-cropped hair, thin moustache; wearing a dark indigo Siamese noble military jacket with gold-trimmed collar and a red sash, the hilt of a Siamese daab sword at his shoulder; calm authority, depicted with great respect, as in a royal temple mural.
items.surasi: Chao Phraya Surasi (Bunma), a Siamese general at about 31, younger brother of Chao Phraya Chakri: energetic, fierce, bold face, short-cropped hair, light moustache; wearing a deep red Siamese noble military jacket with gold trim and a dark sash and his right hand raised in a commanding gesture; no sword visible.
items.kawila: Kawila of Lampang, a Lanna (northern Thai) noble warrior at about 33: lean, alert face, keen eyes, hair tied in a small topknot in old Lanna style; wearing a dark Lanna-style jacket with a patterned red-and-black sash.
items.phraya_san: Phraya San, governor of the provincial town of Sankhaburi in 1782, a Siamese provincial noble in his forties: broad weathered face, wary sideways glance, short-cropped hair, thin moustache; wearing a plain long-sleeved Siamese noble jacket in muted ochre with a dark sash, no crown, no regalia.
items.anurak: Krom Khun Anurak Songkhram, a young Siamese prince of the Thonburi court in his twenties, nephew of King Taksin: proud, tense expression, short-cropped hair, clean-shaven; wearing a fitted indigo princely jacket with gold-trimmed collar and a red sash, no crown.
